name: Methionine cycle
summary: Every cell, mostly liver. Methionine is activated to SAM, the universal methyl donor; giving up its methyl leaves SAH, then homocysteine. Homocysteine is either remethylated to methionine (methionine synthase: B12 + 5-methyl-THF from the folate cycle) or leaves by transsulfuration to cysteine (cystathionine β-synthase and γ-lyase: B6). Homocysteine rises in B12, folate or B6 deficiency and in homocystinuria; methylmalonic acid rises only in B12 deficiency.

met.name: Methionine
met.notes: Essential amino acid. Also a VOMIT source of propionyl-CoA (via α-ketobutyrate).

sam.name: S-Adenosylmethionine
sam.notes: The universal methyl donor: DNA and histone methylation, norepinephrine → epinephrine (PNMT), phosphatidylcholine and creatine synthesis.

hcy.name: Homocysteine
hcy.notes: ↑ in deficiency of B12, folate or B6, and in homocystinuria. Damages endothelium: atherosclerosis and thrombosis.

cys.name: Cysteine
cys.notes: Made here, so it's not essential unless transsulfuration fails (then it is). Used for glutathione and taurine.

mat.name: Methionine adenosyltransferase
mat.notes: Uses all three phosphates of ATP.

mt.name: Methyltransferases
mt.notes: Many enzymes that move SAM's methyl onto DNA, histones, catecholamines (PNMT, COMT), phospholipids and creatine precursors.

ms.name: Methionine synthase
ms.notes: Needs vitamin B12 (methylcobalamin) to carry the methyl group from 5-methyl-THF to homocysteine. B12 deficiency strands folate as 5-methyl-THF (the methyl-folate trap) → megaloblastic anemia, and homocysteine rises. Nitrous oxide inactivates B12 here.

cbs.name: Cystathionine β-synthase
cbs.notes: Needs B6 (PLP). Deficiency → homocystinuria: ↑ homocysteine and methionine, ↓ cysteine; marfanoid habitus with downward lens dislocation, intellectual disability, osteoporosis, thrombosis and early atherosclerosis. Treat: ↓ methionine, ↑ cysteine, B6 (some respond), B12, folate, betaine.

cgl.name: Cystathionine γ-lyase
cgl.notes: Needs B6 (PLP). Its α-ketobutyrate goes on to propionyl-CoA.
